manual_seed_payload.origin_context: Short-duration Kalshi weather/rain markets motivated leaving unusually favorable passive limit orders rather than paying near-certain 97-99 cent prices.
manual_seed_payload.proof_of_mechanism: Confirmed historical example: Miami hourly-temperature 76F-or-above NO, resting 5 NO at 89 cents, full unexpected fill around 22:58, final settlement NO, cost $4.45, payout $5.00, realized profit +$0.55 (~12.36% ROI). This is not proof of edge.
manual_seed_payload.core_question: Do strict queue-realistic fills of unusually favorable late passive orders occur often enough, and do the filled subset win often enough after settlement and friction, to have positive expected value?
required_kill_tests: profitability only under optimistic fill assumptions

mechanism: Late-settlement passive-liquidity hypothesis in Kalshi weather markets. The hypothesized edge is favorable maker execution conditional on strict queue-realistic fills, not meteorological forecast accuracy.
